claims.summary: For a finite diagram S_0->...->S_D over any field, the minimum terminal dimension of a componentwise-surjective cover E_0->...->E_D with injective structure maps is sum_b beta_b=dim(S_D)+sum_b dim ker(a_b), where beta_0=dim(S_0), beta_b=dim(S_b)-rank(a_(b-1)). The complement construction attains every prefix bound simultaneously.
claims.assessment: Standard finite persistence/projective-cover linear algebra, proved in full and checked by the staged medium reviewer. Only inclusion maps and projections are supplied; Boolean multiplication and source relations need independent lifts. The normalized horizon control costs 2^n-1. Exact checks cover all 256 binary two-arrow diagrams on dimension-two spaces, 1280 conditions.
claims.rationale: Makes the cost of discarded states explicit without claiming a new persistence theorem, source operator construction, or goal advance.
claims.next_action: Use this as a cost ledger only when a source-aware operator lift is supplied; the intrinsic shadow/profile test takes priority.

claims.summary: F2 specialization of Elbaz-Govindasamy-Lu-Tzameret Theorem64/Corollary65: constant-depth arithmetic circuit equations of total description size s, with Boolean axioms, have a polynomial-size CNF encoding whose size-S depth-t general IPS refutation transfers to the equations with size poly(S,s) and depth O(t+Delta). General constant-depth IPS hardness for such fixed input families therefore transfers to CNFs.
claims.assessment: Attributed established import, exact F2 gate/substitution and field-equation proof scope read and reviewed. This is general degree-unrestricted IPS: no preservation of PC degree, multilinearity or Hilbert-likeness is asserted. Constant input depth, polynomial description and Boolean domains matter. No extension-field interpretation of the unary-bit notation is imported, and the restricted multilinear/ROABP lower bounds do not supply the required premise.
claims.rationale: Broadens the algebraic starting families available to the queued IPS alternative, while retaining its unproved unrestricted circuit-size lower bound. No new simulation or goal advance is claimed.
claims.next_action: Look for a qualifying general-IPS-hard algebraic family; do not substitute a near-half PC bound or multilinear IPS bound without a separate implication.

claims.summary: For an arbitrary-field Boolean degree-D pseudoideal J_D and a tuple E_i of degree <=e with e+K<=D, let c(k)=rank(f in V_k -> ([E_i f])_i). If old standard-monomial level j has size <=binomial(X,j) for K-delta<j<=K, X>=K and 1<=delta<=K, then for c(K)>0, c(K-delta)/c(K)>=(1+sum_(i=1)^delta rho^i)^(-1), rho=(X-K+delta)/(K-delta+1). A proved bound on the actual error standard family also suffices.
claims.assessment: Attributed direct extension of the near-half notebook's Kruskal-Katona proof from binary C_D to any Boolean pseudoideal and any coefficient field. Bounded absorption gives a down-closed squarefree standard family; Lovasz shadows give the ratio. The zero-rank case is separate and every weight/prefactor degree is included in e. This does not extend binary rank retention/gain to other fields, and does not assume a source-wide level cap or replace the ratio by the base cumulative Hilbert ratio.
claims.rationale: Useful cross-notebook quantitative criterion, not a new shadow method or an attained main-goal regime. Its calibration respects the existing five-point counterexample.
claims.next_action: Combine with the actual affine-annihilator image profile and check whether its level caps, weight costs and original replay permit a source-derived improvement at arbitrary polynomial inventory.
